$comment: The product's identity, in one file (MX-T7, D-36).
This is the ONLY place the product is named. Everything that carries the
name derives from here: the TypeScript constants in @piorbit/protocol, the
Node build scripts, the vite build, electron-builder.yml, the .desktop
entry, the AppStream metainfo, the web manifest and install.sh. Renaming
the product is one edit to this file plus `pnpm identity:generate`.
Nothing else may write the name. `pnpm identity:check` runs inside
`pnpm -r build` and `pnpm -r test` and fails the build the moment a file
{repository} and {homepage}; the identity module expands them.
When the name changes, move the old identity into formerNames so an
existing install's directories and storage keys are migrated rather than
name: piorbit
$wireNamespace: The namespace on every wire contract, and the one value here that a rename
It appears in the relay's WebSocket subprotocol, the Pi event-bus event
names the companion extension listens on, the `<ns>/…` session-message
types, and the HKDF labels that derive a paired device's channel keys.
Renaming those would silently break every paired phone (two peers would
derive different keys and simply fail to connect), every third-party
extension that emits a panel, and every stored session already on disk.
So it is frozen on purpose. When the product is renamed, `name` changes
and this does not; the day a protocol break is wanted, it gets a version
suffix rather than a new spelling.

copy.summary: A control room for coding agents
copy.description: Runs coding agent sessions across every project on this machine, and mirrors them to your phone.
copy.descriptionMore: Everything is configured inside the window: providers, models, extensions and projects. {displayName} brings its own runtime and its own agent, so there is nothing to install first and nothing on your machine for it to disagree with.
copy.descriptionRelay: The phone is not a second application. It is the same interface, reached over an end-to-end encrypted relay that {displayName} runs itself, so a session left on the desktop is the session picked up on the train.
copy.webDescription: Your coding agents, from anywhere. Answer approvals, steer runs, watch every project.
